newsitem.title: UK: Unilever launches ovulation meter in UK.
newsitem.headline: Unilever launches ovulation meter in UK.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever on Monday launched a meter in Britain that tests the hormones in urine, allowing women to tell whether they can make love without the risk of becoming pregnant.
"The monitor will indicate a green light when a woman is free to make love without using a contraceptive and a red light on the days on which she is at risk of becoming pregnant," Unilever said.

The launch of the ovulation meter, dubbed Persona, will be accompanied by a 5.0 million pound ($7.8 million) promotion campaign. The product is scheduled to be available in over 20 countries in Europe, Australasia and north America by 2000.

Unilever said Persona, developed after 15 years of research at a cost of tens of millions of pounds, allows couples to have sex without using contraceptives most days of the month. It said Persona was 95 percent reliable -- as reliable as condoms. The product consists of a small hand-held monitor and disposable urine test sticks.
"Persona will have a major impact on the lives of many women and their partners," said Leendert Staal, chairman of the Unilever unit that produces the product.
